subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept this official MXC sandbox plugin with `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, native `node-pty`/executor packaging, and upstream `--config-base64` argv transport?
rationale: The remaining dependency and argv transport boundaries affect sandbox security and supply-chain policy, and cannot be safely decided by automated code review alone.

options.title: Accept after narrow repair
options.body: Require the full-registration guard/test first, then approve the exact-head dependency graph if secops accepts the preview SDK and argv transport for this prerelease plugin.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but block merge until MXC provides a non-argv config transport or stronger upstream security guidance.

options.title: Decline first-party packaging
options.body: Close or redirect the plugin if maintainers do not want to own this native Windows sandbox dependency as an official OpenClaw package.

recommendation.title: Accept after narrow repair
recommendation.body: Require the full-registration guard/test first, then approve the exact-head dependency graph if secops accepts the preview SDK and argv transport for this prerelease plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on this PR and introduced the closest OpenShell sandbox plugin precedent.
